title: Conditionals: Real and Hypothetical
summary: Practise first, second and third conditionals and distinguish real possibilities from imagined situations.

explanation.heading: First conditional: real possibilities
explanation.body: Use if + present simple, followed by will + base verb, for possible future results.
explanation.example: If the tests pass, we will release the update.

explanation.heading: Second conditional: hypothetical present
explanation.body: Use if + past simple and would + base verb for unreal or unlikely present/future situations.
explanation.example: If I had more time, I would study another language.

explanation.heading: Third conditional: unreal past
explanation.body: Use if + past perfect and would have + past participle to imagine an alternative past result.
explanation.example: If we had tested earlier, we would have found the bug.

exercises.prompt: If I had more time, I ___ Japanese.
exercises.feedback: Second conditional uses would + base verb for an imagined present situation.

exercises.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ indoors.
exercises.feedback: First conditional: if + present simple, then will + base verb.

exercises.prompt: If I had known about the issue, I ___ you.
exercises.feedback: Third conditional: would have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: If she ___ (be) free tomorrow, she will join us.
exercises.feedback: A first conditional uses present simple after if.
acceptedAnswers: is

exercises.prompt: If we ___ (test) the system earlier, we'd have found the bug.
exercises.feedback: Third conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause.
acceptedAnswers: had tested

exercises.prompt: If I ___ (be) you, I'd check the logs.
exercises.feedback: Were is standard in formal hypothetical advice; was is also used informally.
acceptedAnswers: were
was

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: If I will see him, I will tell him.
exercises.feedback: The if-clause normally uses present simple in a first conditional.
acceptedAnswers: If I see him, I will tell him.
If I see him, I'll tell him.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: If they had left earlier, they would arrive on time yesterday.
exercises.feedback: An unreal past result uses would have + past participle.
acceptedAnswers: If they had left earlier, they would have arrived on time yesterday.
If they'd left earlier, they would have arrived on time yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: If you heat water to 100°C at sea level, it will boils.
exercises.feedback: The zero conditional uses present simple; a first conditional can also use will boil.
acceptedAnswers: If you heat water to 100°C at sea level, it boils.
If you heat water to 100°C at sea level, it will boil.

exercises.prompt: If water reaches its boiling point under constant pressure, it ___.
exercises.feedback: Zero conditional expresses a general scientific result.

exercises.prompt: If the supplier called today, we ___ (ask) for an update.
acceptedAnswers: would ask
exercises.feedback: Second conditional uses would + base verb in the result clause.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: If I had studied more, I would pass the exam last week.
acceptedAnswers: If I had studied more, I would have passed the exam last week.
exercises.feedback: An unreal past result requires would have + past participle.

learningObjectives: Choose zero, first, second, and third conditional patterns.
Separate real possibilities from hypothetical situations.

left.label: First conditional
left.example: If the test passes, we will deploy.

right.label: Second conditional
right.example: If the test passed, we would deploy.

left.label: Second conditional
left.example: If I had more time, I would study.

right.label: Third conditional
right.example: If I had had more time, I would have studied.
right.note: An unreal situation in the past.

examples.sentence: If you press Reset, the controller restarts.
If she calls, I will answer.
examples.note: First conditional: a real future possibility.

examples.sentence: If we had tested it, we would have found the bug.
examples.note: Third conditional: an unreal past result.

commonMistakes.incorrect: If I will have time, I will call you.
commonMistakes.correct: If I have time, I will call you.
commonMistakes.why: Use present simple in a standard first-conditional if-clause.

commonMistakes.incorrect: If I had known, I would tell you yesterday.
commonMistakes.correct: If I had known, I would have told you yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: Third conditional requires would have + past participle in the result.

studyTips: Choose the meaning first: fact, real future, imaginary present, or imaginary past.
The if-clause and main clause may appear in either order.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say what will happen if it rains: you will stay home.
acceptedAnswers: If it rains, I will stay home.
If it rains, I'll stay home.
I will stay home if it rains.
I'll stay home if it rains.
speakingExercises.feedback: A real future possibility uses if + present simple and will + verb.

speakingExercises.prompt: Imagine having more time. Say that you would learn French.
acceptedAnswers: If I had more time, I would learn French.
If I had more time, I'd learn French.
I would learn French if I had more time.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the second conditional for a hypothetical present situation.

speakingExercises.prompt: Imagine you did not know about a bug. Say you would have fixed it if you had known.
acceptedAnswers: If I had known about the bug, I would have fixed it.
If I'd known about the bug, I'd have fixed it.
I would have fixed the bug if I had known about it.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the third conditional for an unreal past situation.
